response_text: Because raw accuracy can't tell a lucky streak from real evidence. Two agents at "100% accurate" and "96% accurate" sound like the first is better — but if the first is 5/5 and the second is 384/400, the Wilson lower bound (ADR-0002) puts the first at roughly 57% and the second at roughly 94%, and the ladder correctly reads the second as the stronger case. A point estimate treats both records as equally certain; the Wilson lower bound is the same proportion adjusted for how much evidence actually backs it, so a small perfect run can't outrank a large, slightly-imperfect one. Everywhere this system decides something automatically — increase eligibility, drift confirmation — it reads the lower bound, never the raw point accuracy, for exactly this reason (System Explained, §3 Glossary; ADR-0002).
